title: Finish the Line Like a Homeric Singer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Complete six Homeric hexameter lines by choosing the name formula for Achilles or Odysseus whose syllables exactly fill the space left at the end of the line.

educational.topic: Homeric oral-formulaic composition and dactylic hexameter
learningObjectives: Use the size of the metrical space left at the end of a line to choose the Homeric name formula that completes it, for six lines naming Achilles or Odysseus, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Practice problems applying Parry's metrical rule, with a to-scale picture of the fit and two attempts per line
keyQuestions: Why is Achilles 'swift of feet' while he sits in his hut?
commonMisconceptions: Homer chose each epithet for its meaning at that moment, so 'swift-footed' means Achilles is running.
The singers memorized a fixed text word for word.
Any adjective could fill any gap.
assessmentOpportunities: Lines composed on the first try (mastery: 5 of 6).
Closing question on the sitting, swift-footed Achilles (not scored).
